scenarios.title: Second Opinion
scenarios.text: The club doctor says surgery and six months. A famous specialist abroad says no surgery, rest and rehab, four months. The club is paying for one of them.

choices.label: Trust the club doctor
choices.text: Surgery goes well. The rehab is long and boring and works.

out.text: The specialist is right. He's back a month early, stronger than before.
The specialist was wrong. He needs the surgery anyway, a month later. Two months lost.

scenarios.title: The Loneliest Room
scenarios.text: Week six of rehab. The squad trains on the pitch outside the window while he does leg raises with a resistance band. Nobody texts any more. The physio is the only person he talks to.

choices.label: Go to every match and every team meal
choices.text: He goes to everything: matches, meals, meetings. The squad starts saving him a seat again.

choices.label: Learn something new
choices.text: He starts an online course and studies the game from the stands. He comes back smarter.

choices.label: Disappear into your phone
choices.text: Hours of scrolling. The comments say he's finished. He starts to believe them.

scenarios.title: One More Pill
scenarios.text: He's been taking painkillers before every training session for a month now. Then before every match. Then before sleep. The bottle is nearly empty. He's already thinking about the next one.

choices.label: Tell the club doctor everything
choices.text: The doctor takes it seriously and kindly. A plan, a taper, physio for the real problem. It takes two months. He's clean, and the knee is better.

choices.label: Keep going, carefully
choices.text: He keeps going. It gets harder to stop. Eventually he can't hide it any more.

scenarios.title: Running on Empty
scenarios.text: He sits in the car outside the training ground for forty minutes and can't make himself go in. His hands are shaking. Nothing is wrong, and everything is wrong.

choices.label: Tell the club and ask for time off
choices.hint: Some will judge. Many will respect it.
choices.text: The club gives him two weeks. A psychologist, rest, home cooking. He comes back lighter. A month later, two teammates ask for the psychologist's number.

choices.label: Start seeing a psychologist quietly
choices.text: Weekly sessions with someone who doesn't care about football. Slowly the shaking stops.

choices.label: Push through
choices.text: He pushes through. It gets worse before it gets anything else.

scenarios.title: Say It Out Loud
scenarios.text: A journalist he trusts asks whether he'd talk publicly about his mental health, the therapy, the panic in the car park. 'It might help someone,' she says.
scenarios.prompt: Talk publicly about your mental health?

choices.label: Yes, all of it
choices.text: The interview is honest and gentle. Thousands of messages arrive from young players and fans. One says, 'You saved me.' He keeps that one.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.text: Not yet, he says. Maybe one day.

scenarios.title: Seeing Double
scenarios.text: A clash of heads in the match. He played on. Now, hours later, the lights are too bright, he's nauseous, and he can't remember the drive home.

choices.label: Tell the doctor and follow the protocol
choices.text: The protocol is strict: dark rooms, no screens, slow return. Two weeks out. His head is clear when he comes back.

choices.label: Hide it and play the next match
choices.hint: Brains are not to be gambled with.
choices.text: He hides it. In the next match he can't follow the ball. He's subbed at half-time and diagnosed properly. Now it's a month.

scenarios.title: The Mirror
scenarios.text: In the dressing room, everyone seems bigger, stronger, more defined. A teammate jokes about his skinny legs. He starts looking at supplements online late at night, some of them sketchy.

choices.label: Ask the club's strength coach for a plan
choices.text: A proper plan: food, sleep, lifting. Six months later the jokes stop.

choices.label: Order the supplements
choices.hint: Some of those products aren't legal.

out.text: He reads the label properly and sends them back. Close call.
One of them contains a banned substance. A random test. A ban.

scenarios.title: 3am
scenarios.text: He hasn't slept more than four hours a night for two weeks. His reactions in training are slow. The sports scientist's data screams it.

choices.label: A sleep specialist
choices.text: The specialist bans screens after 9pm and coffee after noon. It's miserable for a week, then he sleeps like a child.

choices.label: Sleeping pills
choices.text: He sleeps. He also wakes up foggy for training. Not quite a solution.

scenarios.title: First Tackle Back
scenarios.text: He's fit. The scans say so. The physio says so. But in his first training match back, a tackle comes in and he pulls out of it, flinching. Everyone saw.
scenarios.prompt: You're scared after a long injury.

choices.label: Talk to the club psychologist
choices.desc: The fear is normal. Deal with it.
choices.hint: The head heals slower than the body.
choices.text: The psychologist helps him trust the knee again. A month later, he goes into a fifty-fifty without thinking. He's back.

choices.label: Force yourself
choices.text: He forces himself into every challenge. It's tense, then it isn't.

scenarios.title: Food Poisoning
scenarios.text: Something from the team hotel buffet. Half the squad is ill. He's spent the night on the bathroom floor. Kick-off is in eleven hours.

choices.label: Tell the doctor you can't play
choices.text: He sits out. The team, weakened, loses. Nobody blames him.

out.text: He plays on willpower and nothing else. The manager calls it the bravest performance of the season.
He's subbed after thirty minutes, grey and shaking.

scenarios.title: The Knee
scenarios.text: A specialist looks at his MRI for a long time. 'The cartilage is wearing thin. You have a few good years left if you manage it. One if you don't.'
scenarios.prompt: Your knee has a time limit.

choices.label: Manage it: fewer minutes, more care
choices.text: Rest days, injections, a reduced load. He plays fewer matches and has more years.

choices.label: Ignore it, play every game
choices.text: He plays every minute. The knee aches every morning. He doesn't tell anyone how much.

scenarios.title: A New Diet
scenarios.text: A famous teammate swears his career was extended by going fully plant-based. He offers to share his chef. The club nutritionist is curious. {MUM} is horrified.

out.text: Three months later: lighter, faster recovery, fewer aches. He sticks with it. {MUM} sends meat anyway.
He feels weak and hungry all the time. He goes back to normal and eats {MUM}'s cooking for a week straight.

choices.label: No thanks
choices.text: He declines. {MUM} is very relieved.

scenarios.title: The Heat
scenarios.text: Forty degrees at kick-off. In the second half, the pitch starts to spin. He finds himself on his knees without knowing how he got there.

choices.label: Signal and come off
choices.text: He comes off, gets ice and fluids. The doctor says another ten minutes could have been serious.

choices.label: Stay on
choices.text: He collapses in the 80th minute. Hospital, drips, a week of rest. The club changes its hydration plan.

scenarios.title: The Heir
scenarios.text: The club has signed a talented young player in {J}'s position: {T}. Everyone knows what it means. The kid is nervous around him, like he's taking something that isn't his.

choices.label: Teach him everything
choices.text: He teaches the kid every trick. When {T} scores his first goal, he runs straight to {J} on the bench. The cameras catch it.

choices.label: Make him earn every minute
choices.desc: Not giving up the shirt yet.
choices.text: He fights for the shirt every day. The kid is better for it. So is he.

choices.label: Freeze him out
choices.text: He's cold to the kid. The squad sees an old man clinging on. It's not a good look.

scenarios.title: The Last Contract
scenarios.text: His contract is running out. The club offers one more year on a big pay cut, as a squad player. A club in a smaller league offers two years, decent money and a starting place.
scenarios.prompt: Your last big decision as a player.

choices.label: Stay, as a squad player
choices.text: He stays. He plays less and coaches more. The fans give him a standing ovation every time he warms up.

choices.label: Go where you'll play
choices.desc: Your legs have more to give.
choices.text: He tells his agent to take the smaller club's offer. A last adventure.

choices.label: Start thinking about retirement
choices.text: He starts thinking about life after football. It's frightening and a little exciting.

scenarios.title: The Farewell Season
scenarios.text: He's announced that this will be his last season. Every away ground now applauds him. Opponents ask for his shirt. Even the rival ultras made a banner: 'RESPECT'.

choices.label: Soak in every moment
choices.text: He signs every shirt and claps every away end. He keeps a notebook of every moment. It's the happiest season of his career.

choices.label: Focus on winning one last thing
choices.text: He trains like it's his first season. The squad follows his lead.

scenarios.title: The Coaching Job
scenarios.text: The club offers him a job with the under-18s once he retires. A pathway to the first team one day. The money is modest; the meaning is not.

choices.label: Accept
choices.text: He accepts. He's already planning his first training session in his head during matches.

choices.label: Keep options open
choices.text: He thanks them and says he'll think about it. The offer stays on the table.

scenarios.title: A TV Audition
scenarios.text: A TV channel asks him to co-commentate on a match he's not playing in. Just to see. If it goes well, there's a job waiting after retirement.

out.text: He's natural, funny and insightful. The channel offers him a contract on the spot.
He says 'great ball' eleven times. The channel thanks him for his time.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.text: He declines. Still a player, for now.

scenarios.title: A Step Slower
scenarios.text: A twenty-year-old winger runs past him in training like he isn't there. It's never happened before. The kid didn't even look back.

choices.label: Reinvent your game
choices.text: He adjusts: positioning, anticipation, fewer sprints, smarter ones. The kid never gets past him again.

choices.label: Extra fitness work
choices.text: Extra sessions, ice baths, a personal trainer. He holds the clock back, a little.

choices.label: Accept it with humour
choices.text: 'Next time, kid,' he shouts after him. The squad laughs. So does he.

scenarios.title: The Testimonial
scenarios.text: The club wants to hold a testimonial match in his honour: former teammates, old rivals, his family on the pitch at half-time. All the money goes wherever he wants.

choices.label: Yes, and give the money to charity
choices.text: Thirty thousand people. His old managers. {MUM} in tears on the pitch. Every cent goes to children's football in his hometown.

choices.label: Yes, and keep the money for your family
choices.text: A beautiful day. The money secures his family's future. Nobody begrudges him it.

scenarios.title: Dad Legs
scenarios.text: His child wakes up three times a night. He's thirty-something with a newborn and a match on Saturday. His body is not designed for this.

choices.label: Share the nights equally
choices.text: He takes his share of nights. He's exhausted. {Pf} looks at him differently, in the best way.

choices.label: Sleep in the spare room before matches
choices.text: He sleeps in the spare room before matches. {Pf} understands. Mostly.

scenarios.title: The Old Rival Hangs Up His Boots
scenarios.text: {RIVAL}, his great rival for a decade, announces his retirement. In the farewell interview he says {J} was the reason he got better.

choices.label: Send him a message
choices.text: A long message about every battle. {RIVAL} replies with a photo of their first meeting, aged nineteen.

choices.label: Turn up at his farewell match
choices.text: He turns up in the rival's stadium and applauds from the tunnel. The home fans, for once, applaud him back.

scenarios.title: Before It's Over
scenarios.text: {KID} has never seen him play live in a stadium: always on TV, always too young or too far away. There may not be many chances left.
scenarios.prompt: Make sure your child sees you play?

choices.label: Bring {KID} to the next home match
choices.text: {KID} watches from the front row in a shirt with {J}'s name. When he scores, he runs to the front row first.

choices.label: Walk out with {KID} as mascot
choices.text: {KID} walks out holding his hand. Thirty thousand people stand. He has to wipe his eyes before kick-off.

scenarios.title: The Last Dance
scenarios.text: A former manager, now at a club fighting relegation in a lower league, calls. 'I need someone who's been there. Six months. Help me keep them up.'

choices.label: Take it
choices.text: He tells his agent to make it happen. A last adventure, for an old friend.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: He declines kindly. His knees are grateful.

scenarios.title: The Elder
scenarios.text: The young players have started coming to him with everything: contracts, girlfriends, agents, homesickness. He's become the dressing-room elder without noticing.
scenarios.prompt: You're the dressing room's elder now.

choices.label: Embrace it
choices.text: He sets up a WhatsApp group for the young players called 'Ask the Old Man'. It's always busy.

choices.label: Point them to professionals
choices.desc: You're a player, not a therapist.
choices.text: He helps where he can and points them to the club's welfare team for the rest. Sensible.

scenarios.title: And Then What?
scenarios.text: Lying awake: what does a footballer do at thirty-six? Every day for twenty years has been training, matches, travel. In a year or two, the alarm will go off and there'll be nowhere to be.
scenarios.prompt: You're afraid of life after football.

choices.label: Start planning now
choices.text: He starts a business course on Tuesday nights. The fear shrinks a little every week.

choices.label: Talk to retired players
choices.text: Three retired players, three dinners, three honest stories. Two of them struggled badly. One found peace. He learns from all three.

choices.label: Don't think about it
choices.text: He pushes the thought away. It comes back at 3am, as these thoughts do.

scenarios.title: Going Home to Finish
scenarios.text: His first club, {FIRSTCLUB}, wants him back for the last chapter. The money is a fraction of what he earns now. His mother has already told the whole neighbourhood.
scenarios.prompt: Go home to finish your career?

choices.label: Go home
choices.text: He tells his agent: take it. Home.

choices.label: Stay abroad
choices.text: He thanks them warmly and stays. His mother is disappointed, then proud.
